title: Finding a path to the bowl
lead: A Nottingham researcher tested how a robot arm handles changes in where a bowl and plate are set down. At a Tokyo exhibit, visitors can see a tabletop robot respond to voices and gestures.

news.title: A compact controller uses geometry to move a bowl onto a plate
news.summary: Aly Magassouba of the University of Nottingham published a robot control method that uses the position and orientation of objects to choose a gripper motion. After training in simulation, the controller completed 21 of 24 bowl placement trials on physical Franka Panda arms.
news.details: A bowl can be moved across a table, but the gripper still needs a way to reach it. Aly Magassouba of the University of Nottingham trained a controller on one simulated arm and ran it on two physical Franka Panda arms. With the objects shifted between trials, the robots put the bowl on its plate 21 times in 24 attempts, including two that succeeded after a retry.
news.technical_novelty: The program takes object positions and orientations as input. It works with the geometry of the objects relative to each other and to the gripper.
news.engineering_impact: After a missed grasp, the program can plan another move using the new positions of the gripper and bowl.
news.limitations: The real-world test measured one task: putting the bowl on the plate.
news.evidence_status: Author-reported physical feasibility test in a preprint.
news.body:
A bowl can be moved across a table, but the gripper still needs a way to reach it. Aly Magassouba of the University of Nottingham trained a controller on one simulated arm and ran it on two physical Franka Panda arms. With the objects shifted between trials, the robots put the bowl on its plate 21 times in 24 attempts, including two that succeeded after a retry.

The program takes object positions and orientations as input. It works with the geometry of the objects relative to each other and to the gripper. If the bowl is farther away or sits at a different angle, the controller can base its next movement on that difference. The method uses a screw representation, a way to describe rotation and translation together. Perception, the step that determines where objects are, supplies those inputs separately.

The real-world test supplied the same type of geometric scene description as the simulations. On a laptop CPU, computing a control action took 9 milliseconds in a system with a 50-millisecond control period. That timing concerns the controller itself. The accuracy of the upstream scene description remains important because an error there changes the relations from which the controller computes movement.

When the first attempt misses the bowl, the relationship between the hand and the bowl changes. In two trials the program picked up the bowl on a second attempt and finished the job. The result so far covers one task with one kind of placement.

news.title: A tabletop robot opens to visitors and app developers in Tokyo
news.summary: Jizai has put Palmimo DevKit, a programmable tabletop robot, on display at Tokyo Innovation Base. Visitors can talk or wave to it, and the company plans to run apps from developer events on the exhibit after checking operation and safety.
news.details: At Tokyo Innovation Base in Chiyoda, visitors can wave to a small machine and watch how it answers. Jizai opened the free exhibit on November 25. It put a programmable tabletop robot called Palmimo DevKit on the first floor, where it plans to use the same hardware to test new ways of interacting with visitors.
news.technical_novelty: The robot has a camera, a microphone array, a speaker, a round display and six legs. The camera and microphones give its software information about what is happening nearby, while the display, sound and motion allow it to respond.
news.engineering_impact: Developers can change how the robot moves and answers using the same camera, speaker and legs.
news.limitations: Public trials with apps from developer events are planned after checks of operation and safety.
news.evidence_status: The exhibitor reported the opening and describes planned tests of new apps.
news.body:
At Tokyo Innovation Base in Chiyoda, visitors can wave to a small machine and watch how it answers. Jizai opened the free exhibit on November 25. It put a programmable tabletop robot called Palmimo DevKit on the first floor, where it plans to use the same hardware to test new ways of interacting with visitors.

The robot has a camera, a microphone array, a speaker, a round display and six legs. The camera and microphones give its software information about what is happening nearby, while the display, sound and motion allow it to respond. Jizai publishes a software development kit for Python, a set of tools for writing programs for the robot. Programmers can change how the machine interacts with people while keeping the hardware in place.

Jizai scheduled its first developer event for December 10. The company plans to rotate applications on the exhibit after checking their operation and safety. A public setting will let developers observe whether a visitor understands the response without having read an instruction manual before approaching the table.

A conversation and a little walk can come from the same hardware, depending on the program it is running. At the opening, visitors can see the behavior of the software already installed. Apps written at developer events are planned for later, after Jizai has reviewed them.

news.title: A construction robot took materials indoors and up a lift
news.summary: South Korea's GoLe Robotics reported a construction-site trial at an industry meeting on November 25. The robot followed a route from an outdoor loading point on the fifth floor to a lift lobby on the twentieth, and the company described a second trial of automatic loading.
news.details: GoLe Robotics used a November 25 South Korean construction industry meeting to present a practical question: how to get building materials from an outdoor loading point to a floor high inside a hotel. In a trial in Jeongseon on October 28, its transport robot used a route from an outdoor area on the fifth floor to the lift lobby on the twentieth. The route entered the building and used the lift.
news.technical_novelty: Previously, the company had mainly carried boxed floor materials and tiles. The hotel trial plan called for one hundred sacks of dry building mix at 25 kilograms each.
news.engineering_impact: Moving a load between floors required a separate device to connect the transport robot to the lift.
news.limitations: The presentation gives planned time for the hotel trial and no success rate for automatic loading.
news.evidence_status: Vendor presentation describing two field trials, one ongoing on the date of the report.
news.body:
GoLe Robotics used a November 25 South Korean construction industry meeting to present a practical question: how to get building materials from an outdoor loading point to a floor high inside a hotel. In a trial in Jeongseon on October 28, its transport robot used a route from an outdoor area on the fifth floor to the lift lobby on the twentieth. The route entered the building and used the lift.

Previously, the company had mainly carried boxed floor materials and tiles. The hotel trial plan called for one hundred sacks of dry building mix at 25 kilograms each. The slides give about six hours as the planned duration including setup. A separate device attached to the lift handled lift calling and coordination. It was the company's first trial with the loading point outside the building.

The company also described a second site in Gwangmyeong, where it is working with a Hyundai Engineering & Construction robotics team. There, the test centers on loading the vehicle at a station without a worker helping. The schedule on the slides ran from November 2 to 27, extending beyond the day of the presentation.

Moving the sacks between floors required the robot to reach and use the lift. The Gwangmyeong trial asks a different question before the wheels start moving: can the robot collect its load at a station without anyone placing it on the vehicle?

news.title: Panasonic to demonstrate robot coordination and safety tools in Osaka
news.summary: Panasonic Group has announced its program for the RoboNext trade show in Osaka on December 2–4. It plans to demonstrate control of multiple robots, collision assessment and software that generates sequences of robot actions.
news.details: Panasonic Group plans to show how several robots can work under coordinated control and how users can assess their safety at RoboNext in Osaka. The program released on November 25 includes control software, simulation tools and emergency stopping equipment. The company says its December 2–4 exhibit will include demonstrations with physical robot arms and a simulation of collisions.
news.technical_novelty: One part of the exhibit covers Robo Sync, a software platform for controlling and linking robots. Panasonic says visitors will see real robot arms in a demonstration of coordination and control.
news.engineering_impact: Coordinating several robots and assessing their safety call for different tools.
news.limitations: The show program does not specify how generated actions would be checked before they run on real machinery.
news.evidence_status: Company announcement of planned trade show demonstrations.
news.body:
Panasonic Group plans to show how several robots can work under coordinated control and how users can assess their safety at RoboNext in Osaka. The program released on November 25 includes control software, simulation tools and emergency stopping equipment. The company says its December 2–4 exhibit will include demonstrations with physical robot arms and a simulation of collisions.

One part of the exhibit covers Robo Sync, a software platform for controlling and linking robots. Panasonic says visitors will see real robot arms in a demonstration of coordination and control. A separate demonstration will cover generative AI, software that can produce new output from input conditions. Panasonic says it will use this technique to generate robot skills and scenarios, meaning individual actions and sequences for a robot to perform.

The safety section lists a collision simulator, services for evaluating robots that operate alongside people, and a wireless emergency stop device. Panasonic also lists a module for controlling a mobile robot, which it says meets IEC 62061. That technical standard sets out requirements for machinery control systems that carry out safety functions.

Creating a new sequence of movements and assessing whether the machine may collide with something are two distinct engineering jobs. The company intends to display a collision simulator alongside its programs for coordinating robots, giving visitors a chance to see how those jobs differ.

news.title: US adds seven Southeast Asian firms to its export control list
news.summary: The US Commerce Department published a rule on November 25 adding seven firms in Malaysia, Singapore and Thailand to a list that triggers extra export licensing requirements. It includes Singapore's Megaspeed, which Reuters and Time have linked to purchases of NVIDIA computing equipment.
news.details: The US Bureau of Industry and Security added seven firms in three Southeast Asian countries to the Entity List, which triggers extra export controls when listed entities participate in covered transactions. The final rule was published on November 25. It names Megaspeed International in Singapore. In a filing with the US Securities and Exchange Commission, NVIDIA says its board reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive on November 22.
news.technical_novelty: The listings require a license for transactions involving the firms and items subject to US export rules. The published policy is a presumption of denial, meaning the review starts from the position that a license should be denied.
news.engineering_impact: Licensing for covered shipments of computing equipment depends on which companies participate in the transaction.
news.limitations: The rule concerns named firms and items covered by US export controls.
news.evidence_status: Official export control rule, supplemented by separate Reuters and Time reporting.
news.organization: U.S. Bureau of Industry and Security
news.body:
The US Bureau of Industry and Security added seven firms in three Southeast Asian countries to the Entity List, which triggers extra export controls when listed entities participate in covered transactions. The final rule was published on November 25. It names Megaspeed International in Singapore. In a filing with the US Securities and Exchange Commission, NVIDIA says its board reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive on November 22.

The listings require a license for transactions involving the firms and items subject to US export rules. The published policy is a presumption of denial, meaning the review starts from the position that a license should be denied. The controls also cover specified reexports and transfers within a country. In projects that need computing equipment to train or test robot models, the obligations can therefore depend on the organizations involved in the supply chain and which one would receive the equipment.

The bureau cites the risk of advanced computing items being diverted. Time separately examined Megaspeed's historical ownership structure, while Reuters reported on the US debate over chip shipments following Huang's return. The rule sets out requirements for transactions involving the named firms. It contains no finding of personal liability against Huang.

A chip can pass through several companies between the factory and the data center that uses it. The US rule names the companies that now trigger additional license requirements. It applies to those entities rather than every buyer in the three countries.

technology_signal.title: The arm chooses its motion from object positions
technology_signal.summary: A University of Nottingham controller was given the positions and orientations of a bowl and plate. Physical robot arms succeeded in 21 out of 24 trials.
technology_signal.implications: Two successful runs began with a missed grasp. The finding comes from a single task with a bowl and plate.
